newsitem.title: USA: Connie Lee Insurance says Sockwell resigns.
newsitem.headline: Connie Lee Insurance says Sockwell resigns.

text.p: Connie Lee Insurance Co. said Friday Oliver Sockwell, the bond insurance company's president and chief executive officer, will resign effective July 1.
Linda Argo, a senior vice president, said an executive search will begin immediately, Argo said.
The U.S. Congress passed legislation last year privatizing Connie Lee, a move completed earlier this year when the Department of Education sold its share of the company.

"I felt an obligation to guide the company through its deregulation and the repurchase of the federal equity," Sockwell, 53, said in a statement announcing his resignation. "Those goals have been accomplished, we had record earnings in 1996, and we've now added a team of experts in our new market sectors."
Sockwell has been with the company since it was created by Congress to insure bonds sold by education bond issuers. The privatization means Connie Lee can now insure bonds in all market sectors.

Sockwell said he plans after leaving Connie Lee to increase his involvement with SF Equity Partners LP, a closely held investment company of which he is a general partner, and to devote himself to educational and community service projects.
